detailed_sections.full_notes: An arithmetic expression is a combination of numbers and operational signs (+, -, *, /). Expressions are separated into terms by addition and subtraction signs. For example, in 4 + (100 / 2), the terms are 4 and (100 / 2). Evaluating terms first simplifies reading and solving complex expressions.

margin_notes.title: Terms and Brackets
margin_notes.content: Brackets group quantities together so they can be treated as a single term inside a larger expression.

detailed_sections.section: 2.2 Algebraic Properties of Addition and Multiplication
detailed_sections.full_notes:
1. Commutative Property of Addition: a + b = b + a. Changing order does not change the sum.
2. Associative Property of Addition: (a + b) + c = a + (b + c). Grouping does not alter the sum.
3. Distributive Property of Multiplication over Addition: a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c.

Subtracting a number is equivalent to adding its additive inverse: a - b = a + (-b). When removing brackets preceded by a minus sign, the sign of every term inside the bracket reverses: -(a + b) = -a - b and -(a - b) = -a + b.

margin_notes.title: Token Model
margin_notes.content: Using positive and negative integer tokens, subtracting a positive token is equivalent to adding a negative token.
